checks.invariant: A publicly reachable API must not sign or verify staff JWTs with a well-known default SECRET_KEY; production_must_be_safe must actually be the active path.
checks.result: Settings.secret_key defaults to change-me-dev-secret. production_must_be_safe rejects that value, strings shorter than 32 characters, SQLite URLs, and empty CORS_ORIGINS only when environment is production or prod. backend/.env.example ships SECRET_KEY=change-me and ENVIRONMENT=development. create_access_token / user_from_access_token HS256-bind to settings.secret_key with no other audience or key-id check. TRUSTED_HOSTS empty disables TrustedHostMiddleware. No source test covers the production validator.

checks.invariant: Documented production topology must not skip the production validator, must not publish an extra management listener, and must not attach unused third-party secrets to the worker identity.
checks.result: DEPLOY.md first-time order deploys the API with ENVIRONMENT=development so CORS_ORIGINS can be empty, then tells the operator to Generate domain on the API. Dockerfile.api and Procfile bind uvicorn to 0.0.0.0. Worker image has no HTTP server; DEPLOY.md says copy API variables including DATABASE_URL, GOOGLE_API_KEY, R2_*, and SECRET_KEY, and not to attach a public domain. Which Railway service uses which Dockerfile, whether the worker has a public domain, and live env values are not in source. R2 is documented as a private bucket using an Account API token on both API and worker.

checks.invariant: Anonymous internet callers must not reach FastAPI docs, ReDoc, or openapi.json on the production API unless an attached ingress control strips those paths.
checks.result: FastAPI(title=settings.app_name) leaves default docs_url, redoc_url, and openapi_url enabled in every environment, including production. Nothing in config.py or main.py disables them. The API container/Procfile listen on 0.0.0.0. Whether Railway or another proxy currently exposes those paths is not source-visible.

checks.invariant: Released API/worker/web images must resolve only review-pinned base layers, lockfiles, and model bytes.
checks.result: API and worker FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm (floating tag) and pip install -r requirements.txt where every package is a lower bound only (no pip lock). Dockerfile.api then runs rembg new_session('u2netp'), which downloads model bytes at build with no digest pin. Worker installs rembg the same way but does not prefetch the model. Web uses npm ci plus package-lock.json (JS deps pinned) but FROM node:22-bookworm-slim is also a floating tag. Host may use Dockerfile or Procfile/Nixpacks; that choice is not in source.

checks.invariant: Field phones on the production EAS channel must load JS that is bound to a reviewed git digest and a repo-controlled promotion gate.
checks.result: eas.json production.channel is production with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE baked at EAS build time. app.json runtimeVersion 1.1.0, updates.url https://u.expo.dev/dfb4d2a5-1b94-449c-bc28-43466a46803d, checkAutomatically ON_LOAD. No .github workflows exist in the repo, so eas update --channel production is a human/token path not gated by in-repo CI or a git SHA. Who can publish on that Expo project is not source-visible.

checks.invariant: Docker build context must not copy live env files or estate data into the released image.
checks.result: Railway/Docker builds from repo root. .dockerignore excludes .env, backend/.env, *.db, backend/data, and Images. gitignore additionally lists .env.local, .env.production, frontend/.env.local, and mobile/.env, which .dockerignore does not name. Dockerfiles copy requirements/alembic/backend or frontend/ only. No committed live secret file was in those trees; emails in env templates are not secrets. A GitHub-based Railway build would not include gitignored files unless they were committed.

candidates.title: Default JWT SECRET_KEY stays accepted whenever ENVIRONMENT is not production
candidates.description: The production validator refuses weak SECRET_KEY values, SQLite, and empty CORS_ORIGINS, but only after ENVIRONMENT is production or prod. Settings still default SECRET_KEY to a public placeholder, and DEPLOY.md tells operators to bring the API up in development first and to generate a public API domain. If that bootstrap (or a forgotten ENVIRONMENT flip) is what is live, an internet caller can mint HS256 JWTs for any sub and account_id using the documented default. Live Railway env values were not observed.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: production_must_be_safe is skipped for any non-production ENVIRONMENT, while the in-image default SECRET_KEY and backend/.env.example placeholder remain valid in that mode, and deploy docs start the public API in that mode.

trace.description: Documented first deploy sets ENVIRONMENT=development on the API so CORS_ORIGINS is not required, then later generates a public API domain.
SECRET_KEY defaults to the well-known placeholder change-me-dev-secret when unset.
If environment is not production or prod, the function returns without rejecting weak keys, SQLite, or missing CORS_ORIGINS.
Access tokens are HS256-signed with settings.secret_key; verification uses the same key and does not bind an audience.

evidence.description: Env template sets SECRET_KEY=change-me, which production_must_be_safe would reject only after ENVIRONMENT=production.
Weak-key set includes empty, change-me, and change-me-dev-secret, plus any secret shorter than 32 characters.
user_from_access_token decodes HS256 with settings.secret_key and trusts sub plus account_id from the payload.
The later variables table asks for a long SECRET_KEY, but that check is not enforced until ENVIRONMENT is switched to production.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox was available, so a local dummy JWT forge against the default key was not executed.
Live Railway API ENVIRONMENT and SECRET_KEY were not observed; this run must not probe Railway.
Whether the operator already set a long random SECRET_KEY during the development bootstrap is a host-dashboard fact.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated empty-env sandbox, start the FastAPI app with ENVIRONMENT=development and unset SECRET_KEY, mint a dummy HS256 token with the documented default key for a dummy user_id and account_id, and confirm user_from_access_token accepts it. Repeat with ENVIRONMENT=production and confirm startup raises.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects the Railway API service variables only: if ENVIRONMENT is not production/prod, or SECRET_KEY equals a documented placeholder, treat the issue as live. Do not send traffic to the public hostname.

candidates.title: FastAPI docs and OpenAPI remain enabled on the 0.0.0.0 API bind
candidates.description: The API app is constructed with FastAPI defaults, so /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json are registered in development and production. Docker and Procfile bind uvicorn on 0.0.0.0, and DEPLOY.md publishes an API domain for /health. Those routes disclose the full management surface (auth, R2 migrate, admin delete, CT Seller, Facebook). Whether a Railway edge or other proxy currently blocks them is not in source and was not probed.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: FastAPI() is created without docs_url, redoc_url, or openapi_url disabled, and no production overlay or ingress manifest in repo strips those paths before the public bind.

trace.description: app = FastAPI(title=settings.app_name) keeps default documentation and OpenAPI URLs for every environment.
Production startup checks SECRET_KEY, SQLite, and CORS_ORIGINS but does not disable docs or require TRUSTED_HOSTS.
Container starts uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0, so any attached public domain forwards to the default docs routes unless a proxy blocks them.

evidence.description: No docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, or openapi_url=None on the FastAPI constructor.
Nixpacks/Procfile path also runs uvicorn on 0.0.0.0 bound to $PORT.
Operators are told to generate a public API domain and to hit /health on that hostname.
TrustedHostMiddleware is added only when TRUSTED_HOSTS is non-empty; empty is the documented default.

blockers: Live Railway ingress, private-networking flags, and any path filter in front of the API are not in this repo.
This run must not fetch the public API /docs or /openapi.json.
No sandbox was available to boot uvicorn locally and observe the default routes.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated loopback sandbox, start app.main:app and confirm unauthenticated GET /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json return 200 with the operation list. That only proves the application route, not live exposure.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner, from the Railway dashboard or an already-authorized admin path, notes whether the API service has a public domain and whether an edge rule denies /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json. Do not probe the hostname from this agent.

candidates.title: API and worker images consume floating base tags, unpinned PyPI specs, and an unsigned rembg model
candidates.description: Each Docker rebuild of Dockerfile.api and Dockerfile.worker runs pip install against requirements.txt lower bounds and pulls python:3.12-slim-bookworm by tag. The API image additionally downloads the rembg u2netp model during build with no checksum. A PyPI or registry publisher who can change a matching version, retag the base image, or replace the rembg model bytes can land code or weights in the next Railway image. Web JS is lockfiled via npm ci; the Node base tag is still floating. Live resolved digests were not observed.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Maintained Dockerfiles treat mutable tags and unbounded pip specs as the release input, and bake a remotely fetched rembg model into the API image without an integrity pin.

trace.description: API image starts from an unpinned rolling distro tag.
Runtime Python dependencies are specified only as >= versions, with no lockfile consumed by Docker.
Build runs pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt then rembg new_session('u2netp'), baking whatever those resolvers return into the image that later runs uvicorn.

evidence.description: Worker uses the same floating python:3.12-slim-bookworm tag and pip install -r requirements.txt without a rembg digest pin.
Web build and runtime use node:22-bookworm-slim by tag; npm ci plus package-lock.json pins JS packages only.
npm ci is the contrasting control: frontend lockfile is copied and used, unlike Python.
Production images are built from repository root using these Dockerfiles, or optionally Procfile/Nixpacks, on each git push.

blockers: Resolved image digests and pip freeze output on Railway are not in source.
No sandbox was available to perform an offline lock comparison or to hash the rembg model.
This run must not pull Docker Hub, PyPI, or rembg model URLs.

validation_plan.local: In a network-disabled sandbox with vendored wheels, fail the Docker build if unpinned specs cannot resolve, or compare a committed pip freeze to the Dockerfile install. Record base-image and rembg file digests from a once-fetched local cache.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner exports the deployed image digest and a pip freeze from the running API and worker, and confirms whether Railway is on Dockerfile.api versus Procfile. Do not retag or republish.

candidates.title: Production EAS Update channel can replace phone JS without an in-repo git digest gate
candidates.description: TestFlight/production binaries load JS from the Expo updates URL for project dfb4d2a5-1b94-449c-bc28-43466a46803d on channel production, with checkAutomatically ON_LOAD and runtimeVersion 1.1.0. The repo has no GitHub Actions to build, attest, or promote that payload from a git SHA. Anyone who can run eas update --channel production against that project can change field-app behavior independently of git. Expo collaborator lists and token holders were not observed and must not be probed.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The phone updater is bound to a mutable EAS channel name and Expo project URL, not to an in-repo immutable digest or CI promotion workflow.

trace.description: EAS production profile publishes to channel production.
Enabled updates.url points at u.expo.dev for this project, checkAutomatically ON_LOAD, fallbackToCacheTimeout 0.
Installed 1.1.0 binaries accept any update Expo serves for that runtime and production channel, with no in-repo workflow binding the bundle to a git commit.

evidence.description: updates.checkAutomatically is ON_LOAD so a published channel payload is applied at app start.
Production EAS build.env pins EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE to the Railway API; eas update is a separate publish path that does not require this repo's CI.
Server updates are git-push rebuilds; mobile OTA is not described as a digest-pinned promotion in that deploy path, and no .github workflows exist in scope.

blockers: Expo project membership, token scope, and last production-channel publish SHA are account facts, not source.
This run must not call Expo or eas whoami, and must not publish an update.
Whether runtime 1.1.0 binaries are what field phones run is an owner-observed install fact.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner, in the Expo dashboard, lists production-channel publishes against git SHAs, reviews who can run eas update, and confirms runtimeVersion 1.1.0 is the only live binary. Do not publish or roll back from this agent.

hardening: production_must_be_safe does not require TRUSTED_HOSTS, ALLOW_OPEN_REGISTRATION=false, docs disabled, or RUN_CATALOG_JOBS_IN_PROCESS=false.
cors_allow_origins always injects http://localhost:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:3000 even when ENVIRONMENT=production; leftover as a note because credentialed CORS is peer-owned.
DEPLOY.md recommends a Cloudflare R2 Account API token on both API and worker; least-privilege object-prefix keys are not encoded.
Worker is documented to copy SMTP and Meta secrets it does not need for catalog claims; extra env is blast-radius hardening, not a reachable worker HTTP surface in Dockerfile.worker.
.dockerignore omits .env.local and .env.production names that .gitignore already drops; GitHub-context Railway builds still follow gitignore unless those files are committed.
backend/.env.example placeholder SECRET_KEY=change-me is not copied as a live Railway secret, but it matches the weak set and can be pasted into the host UI during the development bootstrap.
